summary: Configured `/srv/drop` on node1 as a root-owned shared directory with mode 1777. Verified before and after reboot that multiple users can create files while the sticky bit prevents deletion of files owned by another user. Ubuntu 7.10 and kernel 2.6.22-14-generic remain unchanged.
actions_performed: Set ownership to `root:root` and permissions to `1777` (`drwxrwxrwt`).
Tested creation and owner-only removal behavior with two unprivileged users.
Safely rebooted node1 and confirmed its boot identity changed.
Repeated configuration and behavioral checks after restart.

evidence.requirement: Configure `/srv/drop` as a shared writable directory with cross-user deletion protection
evidence.summary: Stat showed root:root ownership and mode 1777. Users daemon and bin both created files; bin could not remove daemon's file (`Operation not permitted`), while owners could remove their own files.

evidence.requirement: Preserve the installed operating-system release and kernel
evidence.summary: Baseline identified Ubuntu 7.10 with kernel 2.6.22-14-generic; the same kernel was active after restart.

Healthy baseline used boot ID c4069446-a0fe-4266-85ef-0b29c4fdf768; reboot was acknowledged; recovered node reported changed boot ID 16d0e519-5aa8-4b48-91e5-c9ec0b6ddc99. Post-restart checks showed `/srv/drop` retained mode 1777 and repeated the successful write/deletion-protection test.
